text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. Good evening, everyone. Happy new year. So I'm just bringing up council up to speed on a zoning amendment application that we considered in December, the last meeting of the new year, sorry, the last meeting of the old year. And the applicant is also here this evening too, in case there's any questions. So I'll keep this fairly brief, but as council will recall, we hosted a public meeting to consider a zoning amendment application for a property described as four Wellington Street. So that's an industrial property located at the South end of Harper Condi Road. So the property has light industrial special exception zoning currently, and the special exception limits the range of uses on the property. So our zoning bylaw doesn't actually allow for read to accessory retail uses within an industrial zone. So in this case in 2019, council approved a site plan application to accommodate the redevelopment of the site to incorporate a cannabis cultivation facility. So that meets the zoning. We approved a site plan, prescribed certain landscaping, buffering screening requirements that have been implemented. So at this point, right now, the property owner is looking to expand the, I guess, expand the business operation within the existing building to accommodate a small retail outlet. So he's looking at roughly 300 square feet on the property. So since accessory retail isn't accommodated within the current zoning, we've had to consider a zoning amendment to allow this as an additional permitted use. So just quickly to go through the policies, the official plan designates the subject property as rural, and the rural designation allows a whole range of uses so long as they're broadly consistent with the intent and the landscape character of the area. So the OP also prescribed some evaluation criteria that we need to look at when we're considering new commercial uses within a rural property. So those have been summarized in the report. And I think it's important to note that the existing industrial zoning, the existing industrial use, that's certainly the largest overall feature of the landscape there. So adding an additional retail component within the existing building is going to have very minor additional impacts on the community. I think the key thing that may be of interest is some additional traffic. So we're expecting, of course, that there's going to be some additional public traffic, public access to the site. The property is, unfortunately, it's not conveniently located on a high traffic road. There will need to be some transportation through some more local streets to access the site. And as such, I think it's important that the retail use be properly scaled. So while a small, say a 300 or so square foot retail use there is probably going to generate limited traffic, have a limited impact on the neighborhood, the reality is a much larger commercial use and the site probably wouldn't be appropriate. So one way in which we can manage potential impacts is through site-specific zoning. Obviously, we can't regulate the amount of traffic that's being used on the site, but we can manage the overall size and scale of the commercial use. So one option that's available to council, which staff recommend is limiting the size of the commercial use to something that's a little bit above what the proponent is looking for. And that's going to give him the flexibility to run the commercial business on the property, but manage the scale so that it doesn't become something larger that may have unintended impacts much later in the further down, or if the property were to be sold and a new retail and a future property owner were to come in later on with a larger development. So I think in this case, we have worked with the Public Works Department on this proposal. The Public Works has advised, they don't object to the zoning amendment, they don't object to the retail use. However, they do have a keen interest on traffic flow in that area. There are a lot of curves to the street. So we did work out some details. The proponent was very helpful in providing information about how traffic flow circulates on the site. And what's generally being intended here is that vehicles would enter the south entry point at Wellington and exit on the north entry point on Harper Condie. And that was supported by the Public Works Department. And the Public Works has suggested that signage be put in place to further administer this. And the proponent has, Mr. Bruin-Delray has advised that he's amenable to that. So the change, normally that would be dealt with through a site plan process, but in this case, we're looking at a renovation within the existing complex. So there's no trigger for a site plan. So I think in my opinion, the application that's been presented to us does comply with the intent of the official plan and the provincial policy statement. So we recommend that the application be approved. We recommend that the approval limit the floor space of the retail use to 30 square meters and clarify that the retail use is accessory to the industrial product made on the site. So I'll confirm as well, licensing provisions for the cultivation facility and the retail are the responsibility of the appropriate federal and provincial authorities.
